published_source: Shown only in Figure 4, right panel (ln(permits), balanced composition) of the published article (papers/mksc/mksc.2022.1409.pdf, Articles in Advance p. 10, main text); no printed value. Authors' code output recorded in authors_code_* (aggte dynamic overall ATT over horizons 0..35 from the authors' code on the deduplicated package data, analytic SE; authors_code_n = n_regsample, 90,394 zipcode-months, since the figure prints no N). No value of this path is quoted in the text. Checked Nov 4 2026. Earlier: Figure shows the horizon path of aggte(type='dynamic', min_e=-35, max_e=35, balance_e=35) (repldid.R es_graph with bal=35); published_coef is that aggregation's overall ATT (equal-weight average of horizons 0..35 over the 6 cohorts with >= 35 post months, g <= 180, on the full-sample att_gt) from the authors' code re-run on the deduplicated package data, analytic SE (bstrap=FALSE as in es_graph).
replication_status: exact (exact_code_rerun: the authors' aggte dynamic overall ATT over horizons 0..35 reproduced from their code on the deduplicated package data and recorded in authors_code_*; figure-only, no printed value to compare; Figure 4 is in the main text of the published article, checked Nov 4 2026)
notes: Zipcode-month panel, months 72-215 (Jan 2008-Dec 2019), 755 zipcodes, unbalanced (cities enter the data at different months; two cities exit before Dec 2019). Treatment: binary, absorbing, from the unit-constant timing variable regulation_time (month the short-term-rental regulation took effect; 0 = never; 231 and 246 fall after the sample and are treated as never-treated, as did does). 13 in-sample cohorts (127,150,155,157,173,177,183,198,203,204,210,213,215; 638 zipcodes), 117 never-treated zipcodes (59 never regulated + 58 regulated after Dec 2019), no always-treated units, no switch-offs. Authors report Callaway-Sant'Anna only (did::att_gt, control_group='notyettreated', allow_unbalanced_panel=TRUE, no covariates, no weights, bootstrap SE clustered by zipcode); no TWFE regression exists in the package, the TWFE counterpart is D = 1[regulation_time > 0 & time >= regulation_time] with zipcode FE + month FE, clustered by zipcode. Outcomes are already ln(1+count) in the data file. DATA: the shipped repldid.csv (90,682 rows) has two rows per month for zipcodes 94606 and 94607 in months 72-138 (a second, 144-month series with zero permits), which did 2.5.1 rejects; data_path points to ~/did_packages/_work/mksc.2022.1409/repldid_dedup.csv (90,394 rows), the shipped rows that match the authors' own final-submission repldid.csv (identical file). Project member Davide Proserpio is a coauthor (PROTOCOL Section 6). BALANCED (Figure 4): the authors keep the full-sample att_gt (all 13 cohorts; later cohorts remain not-yet-treated controls) and aggregate with balance_e = 35, so only the 6 cohorts with at least 35 post-treatment months in the data (g <= 215 - 35 = 180: 127, 150, 155, 157, 173, 177; 299 zipcodes) enter the event-study path. Nov 2: the spec now runs on the full sample with balance_e = 35 (field balance_e, implemented in the estimator code) instead of the earlier sample restriction to g <= 180, which had removed the later cohorts as controls. EVENT STUDY (Nov 2 audit): event_structure records the published structure (single horizons -35..35, reference -1, endpoint bins <= -36 and >= 36 for the TWFE counterpart; post summary = equal-weight mean of horizons 0..35 = aggte's dynamic overall ATT). The pipeline's CSA uses the universal base period (post horizons identical to the authors' varying-base path; pre horizons differ).
pipeline_caveat: Nov 2: the pipeline's Callaway-Sant'Anna step is did::att_gt(allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE, control_group = 'notyettreated'), the same unbalanced-panel cells as the authors' code (PROTOCOL 5b revised Nov 2); the composition-fixed cells (units observed in both g-1 and t) are only a diagnostic column (csa_fc). Remaining differences from the published numbers: did 2.5.1 vs the authors' 2022 build, and the deduplicated data (see log).

event_structure.source: repldid.R es_graph() (line 45): aggte(attgt, type='dynamic', min_e=-35, max_e=35, balance_e=bal, na.rm=TRUE, bstrap=FALSE); att_gt line 58, es_graph(..., 35, 35) line 88; event time e = time - regulation_time in months (time = months since Jan 2002); published bins = single horizons -35..35, did's varying base period (e = -1 estimated, post horizons relative to g-1).
event_structure.verified: Authors' published estimator is did::aggte(type='dynamic', min_e=-35, max_e=35, balance_e=35) on att_gt(control_group='notyettreated', allow_unbalanced_panel=TRUE, base_period default 'varying'). Pipeline index: months 72-215 consecutive, rel = t - g equals the authors' e = time - regulation_time for every treated-unit row (0 mismatches); no pre-sample adopters, no always-treated units, adoption after month 215 -> never treated. Pooling the authors' did cells (dedup data, saved att_gt objects) within each single-horizon bin with cohort-size weights over the 6 cohorts with g <= 180 (= balance_e = 35) reproduces the logged aggte path e = -35..35 to 7.2e-16 (did 2.5.1 re-run of repldid.R; varying-base pre horizons included), and the equal-weight mean of horizons 0..35 equals published_coef (-0.123529; diff 2.6e-16). Post horizons are identical under the pipeline's universal base period; the figure's pre-period horizons use did's varying base period, so the pipeline's pre summary (universal base) is not the published pre path. The paper reports no TWFE regression: the TWFE counterpart estimates single-horizon indicators -35..35 (ref -1) with endpoint bins <= -36 and >= 36 (relative times outside the published window are not pooled with the reference, as did does not use them either); this equals the legacy coding (fixest max abs diff to the Nov 1 TWFE paths 5.3e-16 on the legacy g <= 180 sample). Sample: the authors ran on the shipped repldid.csv with the duplicate 94606/94607 series (emulated re-run: dynamic overall differs by ~0.001); the pipeline uses repldid_dedup.csv (90,394 rows; see log).

authors_csa_settings.se: analytic in the figures (bstrap=FALSE in aggte)

legacy_note: legacy_g180_* fields were computed on the superseded sample restriction (6 cohorts g <= 180 plus never-treated, 54,765 rows); y_sd_unweighted_regsample and n_regsample now refer to the full sample (90,394 rows).
csa_weights_note: Nov 2: the published CSA comes from R did (or staggered, whose estimates did reproduces), which weights cells by fixed cohort shares; Hull's DiD-averaging weights cells by treated-observation counts. 'did' reproduces the published number (main analysis, option B); the strict-Hull run (CSA_STRICT_HULL=1, option A) ignores this field.
